limits: Accuracy numbers cover three counties (Wibaux, Petroleum, Park) on one run dated 2026-10-17. They are not a statewide rate.

The reference is the Montana State Library structure point. Its metadata disclaims accuracy; the tested points are almost all Placement Structure, but the metadata read does not say where the point sits relative to the house.
Unit-level rows (63 Wibaux, 17 Petroleum, 1,808 Park) and non-unit rows without a street name or ZIP (3 Wibaux, 4 Petroleum, 39 Park) were not sent. The results describe street-level addresses only.
The parcel-centroid test is a cross-check only: centroids overstate error on parcels over 2 acres.
The TIGER classification uses simple name normalisation (directionals dropped, suffixes mapped). A street-not-found result is an upper bound.
Batch uploads: one 735-row file got no response in 3 min 18 s and was stopped. Chunks of 200 rows with a .csv name returned normally. A file without a .csv name returns HTTP 400.
CORS result is one request with one sample Origin (https://example.github.io). JSONP is documented but was not tested from a browser page.
Only the Census Data API terms page was read for Census terms; no Geocoder-specific terms were found in the pages read.
Nominatim: one search request, as the policy forbids systematic queries; its accuracy was not tested.
Photon: one public API request. No self-hosted Photon or Pelias build was made. The Montana OSM extract size is unknown (Geofabrik unreachable; openstreetmap.fr returned 404).

Index sizes: 959 parcel addresses (two counties) and 11,101 structure-point addresses (one county). The 500,000 figure assumes similar bytes per address. Larger shards compress somewhat better; real lists have more variety (units, suffixes). Sizes are gzip or zlib at level 9, not measured in a browser.
The GitHub Pages check used HEAD requests on the root and one CSS file. No JSON was served from Pages in this workstream.
W6 frequency tables are capped at 200 values. W6 derived housing-unit total is not reconciled here.
The Census benchmark Public_AR_Current may use a TIGER release other than the 2025 files used in the join.
Downloads: about 79.3 MB transferred (the structure-point zip is 65.8 MB, fetched whole), against the 300 MB cap; wall time well inside the 90-minute cap.

Skipped: StructuresFramework_gdb.zip (61,058,458 bytes); TIGER files for the other 53 counties; Geofabrik and the Montana OSM extract; Pelias and Photon builds; Nominatim accuracy sampling; the Census Data API (needs a key, not supplied).
Refuter pass: about 97 MB downloaded (cap 300 MB); TIGER2026 changes the Park no-match split.
open_questions: Which TIGER release backs Public_AR_Current? TIGER2026 is published and changes the Park split; re-run the join once the Current release is known.
Do Census terms for the Geocoder (not found in the pages read) allow a production site, or a server proxy on a visitor's behalf, to batch or query addresses? Is there a request ceiling?
A visitor who types an address sends it off-site if a Census or Nominatim call is made. Nominatim asks users not to submit personal data. What privacy line is needed?
Does the site-files-only rule allow one named off-site geocoder host? That needs an owner decision and a new decision number.
Which D number applies? The globe README uses D32 for storm layers; the imagery brief uses D32 for the USGS imagery exception.
How large is a Montana-only OSM extract (Geofabrik unreachable from this session)? Needed to size a self-hosted Photon or Pelias.
Should the index hold structure points (674,715 statewide per W6, including units) or parcel-linked addresses (497,316 unique ParcelID per W6)?
Montana 2020 housing units: H1 candidate 514,803 from the PL 94-171 file (layout to confirm). The W6 figure 1,084,225 is the population total.
The metadata does not say where a structure point sits relative to the house. A ground check on a few known addresses would settle the house-point accuracy claim.
A proper street-name match (full names with types and aliases) would split the No_Match counts more tightly than this normalisation.
Browser support for DecompressionStream formats beyond gzip is unverified; gzip is the verified one.
Does GitHub Pages serve .json or .gz index shards with gzip on the wire? Only HTML and CSS were checked.

programs.name: U.S. Census Geocoder (single-line and batch)
programs.what_it_gives: Address to latitude and longitude, interpolated on TIGER address ranges; batch up to 10,000 rows per file; benchmark Public_AR_Current. Tested: 82.3% matched on Wibaux structure points, 61.0% Petroleum, 87.9% Park.
programs.cost_or_licence: No cost or key stated in the pages read; batch cap 10,000 rows per file; Data API terms quoted; not endorsed attribution wording in those terms; CORS absent for JSON (JSONP documented).

programs.name: Nominatim public API
programs.what_it_gives: OpenStreetMap place and address search (JSON), with CORS allowed for GET.
programs.cost_or_licence: Usage policy: end-user searches at moderate volume; 1 request per second for all users of the site; no auto-complete; cache results; no bulk. Governed by the policy, not a fee.

programs.name: Photon (self-hosted geocoder)
programs.what_it_gives: OSM-based geocoding and reverse search built on OpenSearch; dumps from the dump server.
programs.cost_or_licence: Apache-2.0. Java 21 or later. Planet database about 95 GB disk and at least 64 GB RAM recommended (README). Planet dump 63,172,802,723 bytes (HEAD).

programs.name: Pelias (self-hosted geocoder)
programs.what_it_gives: Modular geocoder on Elasticsearch 7 or 8; imports OpenAddresses, OSM and Who's on First; Docker set-up for a small area.
programs.cost_or_licence: MIT. Hardware and Montana data size not measured.

programs.name: OpenSearch
programs.what_it_gives: Search engine needed for an external Photon database (OpenSearch 3.x).

programs.name: Option A: precomputed address index as site files (this workstream's build, not a third-party program)
programs.what_it_gives: Client-side lookup from ZIP shards on the same site; no off-site request. Measured: 8.2 to 12.4 bytes per address across layouts and the two tests; about 4.1 to 6.2 MB gzip per 500,000 addresses (see facts); largest statewide ZIP shard about 232 KB (estimate, non-unit rows). Limits: only addresses in the index; unknown addresses must show as not in the index, never as an all-clear.
programs.cost_or_licence: Source terms apply: Montana State Library structure points (disclaimers quoted); TIGER licence not verified; OSM data (ODbL) if used. Owner and mailing fields excluded.

programs.name: OpenStreetMap data
programs.what_it_gives: Address and place data used by Nominatim and Photon.

programs.name: Census TIGER/Line address ranges and EDGES
programs.what_it_gives: Address ranges (FROMHN, TOHN, ZIP) and street names by TLID; used by the Census Geocoder for interpolation. Montana county files about 3.86 MB (TIGER2025) and 3.91 MB (TIGER2026), listed.
programs.cost_or_licence: Licence not verified in pages read.

programs.name: Montana State Library Structures Framework (site address points)
programs.what_it_gives: 674,715 statewide site address points with placement codes; coordinates from the shapefile (DBF coordinates are zero); monthly export.
programs.cost_or_licence: Free download from the Montana State Library FTP; disclaimers quoted; contact geoinfo@mt.gov. No licence sentence found.

programs.name: GitHub Pages (static site hosting)
programs.what_it_gives: Hosts the site files and any index shards; gzip on the wire for HTML and CSS (headers checked).
programs.cost_or_licence: Published site 1 GB maximum; soft bandwidth 100 GB per month; deployments time out after 10 minutes; files over 100 MiB blocked; 10-builds-per-hour soft limit not for custom Actions builds.

programs.name: Browser DecompressionStream (web platform API)
programs.what_it_gives: In-browser gzip decompression of a fetched shard (MDN example uses "gzip").
programs.cost_or_licence: Web platform API; formats beyond gzip not verified.
